ko.title: [물류 101 #4] 왜 당신의 창고는 사실 은행 계좌인가

segments.src: > Inventory is cash sitting on a shelf — and inventory management is the math of deciding how much cash to park there, and when to top it up.
segments.tr: > 재고는 선반 위에 놓인 현금입니다. 그리고 재고 관리는 그곳에 얼마만큼의 현금을 둘지, 언제 보충할지를 결정하는 수학입니다.

segments.src: Every unit in a warehouse is money you already spent but haven't earned back yet.
segments.tr: 창고에 있는 모든 제품 단위는 이미 지출했지만 아직 회수하지 못한 돈입니다.

segments.src: That's why inventory decisions are financial decisions dressed up as operational ones.
segments.tr: 그렇기 때문에 재고 결정은 운영상의 결정으로 포장된 재무적 결정입니다.

segments.src: There are three costs constantly pulling against each other:
segments.tr: 서로 끊임없이 충돌하는 세 가지 비용이 있습니다:

segments.src: - **Ordering cost** — the fixed cost of placing one replenishment order: purchasing labor, freight setup, receiving, inspection. It's roughly the same whether you order 100 units or 1,000.
segments.tr: - **주문 비용(Ordering cost)** — 한 번의 보충 주문을 넣을 때 발생하는 고정 비용: 구매 인건비, 운송 설정, 입고, 검수 등. 100개를 주문하든 1,000개를 주문하든 거의 동일합니다.

segments.src: - **Holding (carrying) cost** — the cost of keeping a unit on the shelf for a year: warehouse space, insurance, shrinkage, obsolescence, and the capital tied up. A common rule of thumb is 20–30% of the item's cost per year.
segments.tr: - **보관 비용(Holding/carrying cost)** — 제품 하나를 1년 동안 선반에 보관하는 비용: 창고 공간, 보험, 재고 손실, 진부화, 그리고 묶여 있는 자본 비용. 보통 제품 원가의 연간 20~30%를 경험칙으로 잡습니다.

segments.src: - **Stockout cost** — the sale you lose, the expedited freight you pay, the customer who goes elsewhere.
segments.tr: - **품절 비용(Stockout cost)** — 놓친 매출, 지불해야 하는 긴급 운송비, 다른 곳으로 떠나버린 고객.

segments.src: Order in big batches and your ordering cost per unit drops, but your shelves fill up and holding cost climbs.
segments.tr: 대량으로 주문하면 단위당 주문 비용은 떨어지지만, 선반이 꽉 차면서 보관 비용이 올라갑니다.

segments.src: Order in small batches and holding cost drops, but you're paying for orders constantly and flirting with stockouts.
segments.tr: 소량으로 주문하면 보관 비용은 떨어지지만, 계속해서 주문 비용을 지불해야 하고 품절 위험을 감수해야 합니다.

segments.src: Inventory management is finding the balance point.
segments.tr: 재고 관리는 그 균형점을 찾는 것입니다.

segments.src: **The EOQ model** answers "how much per order?"
segments.tr: **EOQ 모델**은 "한 번에 얼마나 주문할까?"라는 질문에 답합니다.

segments.src: Economic Order Quantity is the batch size where annual ordering cost and annual holding cost are equal — the bottom of the total-cost curve:
segments.tr: 경제적 주문량(Economic Order Quantity)은 연간 주문 비용과 연간 보관 비용이 같아지는 배치 사이즈로, 총비용 곡선의 가장 낮은 지점입니다:

segments.src: S = cost to place one order ($)
segments.tr: S = cost to place one order ($)

segments.src: H = cost to hold one unit for one year ($)
segments.tr: H = cost to hold one unit for one year ($)

segments.src: Double your demand and EOQ doesn't double — it grows by about 41%.
segments.tr: 수요가 두 배가 되어도 EOQ는 두 배가 되지 않고 약 41% 증가합니다.

segments.src: That's the mathematical reason big retailers hold proportionally *less* inventory than small ones, not more.
segments.tr: 이것이 대형 소매업체가 소규모 업체보다 비례적으로 *더 적은* 재고를 보유하는 수학적 이유입니다.
**안전 재고(Safety stock)**는 "얼마나 완충 장치를 둘까?"라는 질문에 답합니다.

segments.src: EOQ assumes demand and lead times are perfectly predictable.
segments.tr: EOQ는 수요와 리드 타임이 완벽하게 예측 가능하다고 가정합니다.

segments.src: Safety stock is the buffer you carry against that uncertainty:
segments.tr: 안전 재고는 그러한 불확실성에 대비해 보유하는 완충 장치입니다:

segments.src: Safety stock = z * (demand std deviation per day) * sqrt(lead time in days)
segments.tr: Safety stock = z * (demand std deviation per day) * sqrt(lead time in days)

segments.src: The `z` is your chosen **service level** — how often you're willing to be in stock when a customer arrives.
segments.tr: 여기서 `z`는 당신이 선택한 **서비스 수준(service level)**입니다. 즉, 고객이 왔을 때 재고가 있을 확률을 얼마나 설정할 것인가입니다.

segments.src: That jump is the expensive part: going from 95% to 99% costs about 41% more safety stock.
segments.tr: 그 차이가 바로 비용이 많이 드는 부분입니다. 95%에서 99%로 올리려면 약 41% 더 많은 안전 재고가 필요합니다.

segments.src: Chasing 100% costs infinite inventory, which is why nobody sane targets it.
segments.tr: 100%를 쫓으면 무한한 재고가 필요하기 때문에, 제정신인 사람은 아무도 그것을 목표로 하지 않습니다.

segments.src: **The reorder point** answers "when do I order?"
It's the shelf level that triggers a new purchase order:
segments.tr: 새로운 구매 주문을 트리거하는 선반 재고 수준입니다:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: In plain English: enough to cover normal sales while the truck is en route, plus a cushion for the days that aren't normal.
segments.tr: 쉽게 말해, 트럭이 오는 동안의 일반적인 판매량을 충당하고, 평소와 다른 날을 대비한 완충 재고까지 더한 양입니다.

segments.src: Say you run a small e-commerce brand out of Columbus, Ohio, selling an insulated water bottle.
segments.tr: 오하이오주 콜럼버스에서 보온 물병을 판매하는 작은 이커머스 브랜드를 운영한다고 가정해 봅시다.

segments.src: **The numbers:** you sell 12,000 units a year.
Each purchase order from your supplier costs about $75 in labor and paperwork.
segments.tr: 공급업체에 주문을 넣을 때마다 인건비와 서류 작업으로 약 $75가 듭니다.

segments.src: Holding one bottle for a year costs $6 (warehouse space, capital, the risk it goes out of style).
segments.tr: 물병 하나를 1년 동안 보관하는 비용은 $6입니다(창고 공간, 자본, 유행이 지날 위험 등).

segments.src: So about 548 bottles per order, or roughly 22 orders a year — one every two and a half weeks.
segments.tr: 따라서 주문당 약 548개, 즉 연간 약 22번 주문하게 되며, 2.5주마다 한 번꼴입니다.

segments.src: Your combined ordering + holding cost lands near $3,286 a year ($1,643 each, split evenly — that's the signature of being at the EOQ).
segments.tr: 주문 비용과 보관 비용을 합치면 연간 약 $3,286($1,643씩 균등하게 분할 — 이것이 EOQ 상태의 특징입니다).

segments.src: **When to order:** at 300 selling days a year, that's 40 bottles a day.
segments.tr: **주문 시점:** 연간 300일 판매한다고 치면, 하루에 40개씩 팔리는 셈입니다.

segments.src: Your supplier's lead time is 7 days, so you'll sell about 280 bottles while you wait.
segments.tr: 공급업체의 리드 타임은 7일이므로, 기다리는 동안 약 280개가 팔릴 것입니다.

segments.src: Daily demand swings with a standard deviation of about 12 units, and you want a 95% service level:
segments.tr: 일일 수요는 표준 편차 약 12개로 변동하며, 95% 서비스 수준을 원한다면:

segments.src: Now you have a rule a warehouse associate can actually follow: **when the bin hits 333 bottles, order 548 more.** No meetings, no guessing.
segments.tr: 이제 창고 직원이 실제로 따를 수 있는 규칙이 생겼습니다: **재고가 333개가 되면 548개를 추가 주문하세요.** 회의도, 추측도 필요 없습니다.

segments.src: One comforting fact: the total-cost curve near EOQ is remarkably flat.
segments.tr: 한 가지 위안이 되는 사실은, EOQ 근처의 총비용 곡선은 매우 평평하다는 것입니다.

segments.src: Order 20% more than the EOQ — say a 660-unit pallet instead of 548 — and your total cost rises less than 2%.
segments.tr: EOQ보다 20% 더 많이 주문해도(예: 548개 대신 660개들이 팔레트 하나), 총비용은 2% 미만으로 상승합니다.

segments.src: So if your supplier sells in full pallets or offers a volume discount, take the round number.
segments.tr: 그러니 공급업체가 팔레트 단위로 판매하거나 대량 할인을 제공한다면, 그냥 딱 떨어지는 숫자로 주문하세요.

segments.src: EOQ gives you the neighborhood; it doesn't demand precision to the unit.
segments.tr: EOQ는 대략적인 범위를 알려주는 것이지, 개수까지 정확하게 맞출 것을 요구하지 않습니다.
그리고 이 모델의 한계를 알아야 합니다.

segments.src: EOQ assumes steady demand, a fixed lead time, no quantity discounts, and unlimited storage.
segments.tr: EOQ는 일정한 수요, 고정된 리드 타임, 수량 할인 없음, 무제한 저장 공간을 가정합니다.

segments.src: Real life breaks all four — seasonal spikes, port delays, case-pack minimums.
segments.tr: 현실은 이 네 가지를 모두 깹니다 — 계절적 급증, 항구 지연, 최소 주문 수량 등.

segments.src: Treat EOQ as a sanity check on your ordering habits, not as gospel.
segments.tr: EOQ를 절대적인 진리로 보지 말고, 주문 습관을 점검하는 기준으로 삼으세요.

segments.src: 1. Inventory is a tug-of-war between ordering cost (favors big batches) and holding cost (favors small ones); EOQ is where they balance, and it scales with the *square root* of demand.
segments.tr: 1. 재고는 주문 비용(대량 주문 선호)과 보관 비용(소량 주문 선호) 사이의 줄다리기입니다. EOQ는 이 둘이 균형을 이루는 지점이며, 수요의 *제곱근*에 비례합니다.

segments.src: 2. Safety stock buys protection against uncertainty, and the price of that protection rises steeply as you approach 100% service — 95% to 99% costs about 41% more stock.
segments.tr: 2. 안전 재고는 불확실성에 대한 보호막을 제공하지만, 100% 서비스 수준에 가까워질수록 그 보호 비용은 가파르게 상승합니다. 95%에서 99%로 올리는 데 약 41% 더 많은 재고가 필요합니다.

segments.src: 3. The reorder point turns all of it into one simple floor-level rule: demand during lead time, plus your cushion.
segments.tr: 3. 재주문점은 이 모든 것을 하나의 간단한 현장 규칙으로 바꿉니다: 리드 타임 동안의 수요에 완충 재고를 더하는 것입니다.

segments.src: **Q1.** Your supplier streamlines the process and your ordering cost `S` drops to one-quarter of what it was.
segments.tr: **Q1.** 공급업체가 프로세스를 간소화하여 주문 비용 `S`가 기존의 1/4로 줄었습니다.

segments.src: All else equal, what happens to EOQ?
segments.tr: 다른 조건이 동일하다면, EOQ는 어떻게 될까요?

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) Raising your target service level from 95% to 99% increases required safety stock by only about 4%.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) 목표 서비스 수준을 95%에서 99%로 높이면 필요한 안전 재고는 약 4%만 증가한다.

segments.src: **Q3.** Your average daily demand is 50 units, lead time is 6 days, and safety stock is 80 units.
segments.tr: **Q3.** 평균 일일 수요는 50개, 리드 타임은 6일, 안전 재고는 80개입니다.

segments.src: - **Ordering cost (S)** — the fixed cost of placing and receiving one replenishment order, largely independent of order size.
segments.tr: - **주문 비용(Ordering cost, S)** — 한 번의 보충 주문을 넣고 받는 데 드는 고정 비용으로, 주문 크기와는 거의 무관함.

segments.src: - **Holding cost (H)** — the annual cost of keeping one unit in stock: space, capital, insurance, shrinkage, and obsolescence.
segments.tr: - **보관 비용(Holding cost, H)** — 제품 하나를 재고로 유지하는 연간 비용: 공간, 자본, 보험, 재고 손실, 진부화 비용.

segments.src: - **EOQ (Economic Order Quantity)** — the order size that minimizes total ordering plus holding cost, equal to `sqrt(2DS/H)`.
segments.tr: - **EOQ (경제적 주문량)** — 총 주문 비용과 보관 비용을 최소화하는 주문량으로, `sqrt(2DS/H)`와 같음.

segments.src: - **Safety stock** — extra inventory held to absorb demand and lead-time variability, sized by your chosen service level.
segments.tr: - **안전 재고(Safety stock)** — 수요와 리드 타임의 변동성을 흡수하기 위해 보유하는 추가 재고로, 선택한 서비스 수준에 따라 크기가 결정됨.

segments.src: - **Reorder point (ROP)** — the stock level that triggers a new order: expected demand during lead time plus safety stock.
segments.tr: - **재주문점(Reorder point, ROP)** — 새로운 주문을 트리거하는 재고 수준: 리드 타임 동안의 예상 수요에 안전 재고를 더한 값.

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** EOQ moves with the square root of S, so cutting S to 1/4 cuts EOQ to sqrt(1/4) = 1/2.
segments.tr: *정답: **Q1 — B.** EOQ는 S의 제곱근에 비례하므로, S를 1/4로 줄이면 EOQ는 sqrt(1/4) = 1/2로 줄어듭니다.

segments.src: You'd order half as much, twice as often.
segments.tr: 절반의 양을 두 배 더 자주 주문하게 됩니다.

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** The z-value goes from 1.65 to 2.33, so safety stock rises about 41%, not 4%.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (거짓).** z-값은 1.65에서 2.33으로 변하므로, 안전 재고는 4%가 아니라 약 41% 증가합니다.

segments.src: The last few points of service level are always the costliest.
segments.tr: 서비스 수준을 마지막 몇 퍼센트 올리는 것이 항상 가장 비용이 많이 듭니다.

segments.src: > Inventory is cash sitting on a shelf — and inventory management is the math of deciding how much cash to park there, and when to top it up.
segments.tr: > 库存就是放在货架上的现金——而库存管理就是决定在该处存放多少现金以及何时补充的数学问题。

segments.src: Every unit in a warehouse is money you already spent but haven't earned back yet.
segments.tr: 仓库里的每一件商品都是你已经花出去但尚未赚回来的钱。

segments.src: That's why inventory decisions are financial decisions dressed up as operational ones.
segments.tr: 这就是为什么库存决策本质上是披着运营外衣的财务决策。

segments.src: There are three costs constantly pulling against each other:
segments.tr: 有三种成本在不断地相互拉扯：

segments.src: - **Ordering cost** — the fixed cost of placing one replenishment order: purchasing labor, freight setup, receiving, inspection. It's roughly the same whether you order 100 units or 1,000.
segments.tr: - **订购成本** — 下达一次补货订单的固定成本：采购人工、货运设置、收货、检验。无论你订购 100 件还是 1,000 件，这笔费用大致相同。

segments.src: - **Holding (carrying) cost** — the cost of keeping a unit on the shelf for a year: warehouse space, insurance, shrinkage, obsolescence, and the capital tied up. A common rule of thumb is 20–30% of the item's cost per year.
segments.tr: - **持有（仓储）成本** — 将一件商品在货架上存放一年的成本：仓库空间、保险、损耗、过时风险以及占用的资金。一个常见的经验法则是每年占商品成本的 20–30%。

segments.src: - **Stockout cost** — the sale you lose, the expedited freight you pay, the customer who goes elsewhere.
segments.tr: - **缺货成本** — 你失去的销售额、支付的加急运费、流失到别处的客户。

segments.src: Order in big batches and your ordering cost per unit drops, but your shelves fill up and holding cost climbs.
segments.tr: 大批量订购会降低单位订购成本，但货架会塞满，持有成本随之攀升。

segments.src: Order in small batches and holding cost drops, but you're paying for orders constantly and flirting with stockouts.
segments.tr: 小批量订购会降低持有成本，但你必须不断支付订购费用，且面临缺货风险。

segments.tr: 库存管理就是寻找这个平衡点。

segments.tr: **EOQ 模型**回答了“每次订多少？”的问题

segments.tr: 追求 100% 的服务水平需要无限的库存，这就是为什么理智的人都不会以此为目标。

segments.src: **The reorder point** answers "when do I order?"
segments.tr: **再订货点**回答了“我什么时候订货？”的问题

segments.src: It's the shelf level that triggers a new purchase order:
segments.tr: 它是触发新采购订单的货架库存水平：

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: In plain English: enough to cover normal sales while the truck is en route, plus a cushion for the days that aren't normal.
segments.tr: 通俗地说：在卡车运输途中足以覆盖正常销售的库存量，再加上应对非正常日子的缓冲量。

segments.src: Say you run a small e-commerce brand out of Columbus, Ohio, selling an insulated water bottle.
segments.tr: 假设你在俄亥俄州哥伦布市经营一个小型电子商务品牌，销售一款保温水杯。

segments.src: **The numbers:** you sell 12,000 units a year.
segments.tr: **数据：** 你每年销售 12,000 个。

segments.src: Each purchase order from your supplier costs about $75 in labor and paperwork.
segments.tr: 供应商的每份采购订单的人工和文书成本约为 $75。

segments.src: Holding one bottle for a year costs $6 (warehouse space, capital, the risk it goes out of style).
segments.tr: 持有单个水杯一年的成本为 $6（仓库空间、资金、过时风险）。

segments.src: So about 548 bottles per order, or roughly 22 orders a year — one every two and a half weeks.
segments.tr: 所以每次订购约 548 个，或者说每年大约 22 次订单——每两周半一次。

segments.src: Your combined ordering + holding cost lands near $3,286 a year ($1,643 each, split evenly — that's the signature of being at the EOQ).
segments.tr: 你的订购成本 + 持有成本合计每年约为 $3,286（各占 $1,643，平分——这就是处于 EOQ 的标志）。

segments.src: **When to order:** at 300 selling days a year, that's 40 bottles a day.
segments.tr: **何时订货：** 按每年 300 个销售日计算，每天销售 40 个。

segments.src: Your supplier's lead time is 7 days, so you'll sell about 280 bottles while you wait.
segments.tr: 供应商的提前期是 7 天，所以你在等待期间会卖出约 280 个。

segments.src: Daily demand swings with a standard deviation of about 12 units, and you want a 95% service level:
segments.tr: 日需求量的标准差约为 12 个，且你想要 95% 的服务水平：

segments.src: Now you have a rule a warehouse associate can actually follow: **when the bin hits 333 bottles, order 548 more.** No meetings, no guessing.
segments.tr: 现在你就有了一个仓库员工真正可以遵循的规则：**当库存降至 333 个时，再订购 548 个。** 无需开会，无需猜测。

segments.src: One comforting fact: the total-cost curve near EOQ is remarkably flat.
segments.tr: 一个令人欣慰的事实是：EOQ 附近的成本曲线非常平缓。

segments.src: Order 20% more than the EOQ — say a 660-unit pallet instead of 548 — and your total cost rises less than 2%.
segments.tr: 比 EOQ 多订 20%——比如订 660 个而不是 548 个——你的总成本只会增加不到 2%。

segments.src: So if your supplier sells in full pallets or offers a volume discount, take the round number.
segments.tr: 所以如果供应商按整托盘销售或提供批量折扣，直接取整即可。

segments.src: EOQ gives you the neighborhood; it doesn't demand precision to the unit.
segments.tr: EOQ 给你的是一个大概范围；它不需要精确到个位数。
同时也要了解该模型的局限性。

segments.src: EOQ assumes steady demand, a fixed lead time, no quantity discounts, and unlimited storage.
segments.tr: EOQ 假设需求稳定、提前期固定、没有数量折扣且存储空间无限。

segments.src: Real life breaks all four — seasonal spikes, port delays, case-pack minimums.
segments.tr: 现实生活打破了所有这四点——季节性高峰、港口延误、包装箱起订量。

segments.src: Treat EOQ as a sanity check on your ordering habits, not as gospel.
segments.tr: 将 EOQ 视为你订货习惯的理性检查，而不是金科玉律。

segments.src: 1. Inventory is a tug-of-war between ordering cost (favors big batches) and holding cost (favors small ones); EOQ is where they balance, and it scales with the *square root* of demand.
segments.tr: 1. 库存是订购成本（倾向于大批量）和持有成本（倾向于小批量）之间的拉锯战；EOQ 是两者的平衡点，且随需求的*平方根*变化。

segments.src: 2. Safety stock buys protection against uncertainty, and the price of that protection rises steeply as you approach 100% service — 95% to 99% costs about 41% more stock.
segments.tr: 2. 安全库存能抵御不确定性，但这种保护的成本随着你接近 100% 的服务水平而急剧上升——从 95% 提升到 99% 需要多出约 41% 的库存。

segments.src: 3. The reorder point turns all of it into one simple floor-level rule: demand during lead time, plus your cushion.
segments.tr: 3. 再订货点将这一切转化为一个简单的底层规则：提前期内的需求量加上你的缓冲量。

segments.src: **Q1.** Your supplier streamlines the process and your ordering cost `S` drops to one-quarter of what it was.
segments.tr: **Q1.** 供应商简化了流程，你的订购成本 `S` 降至原来的四分之一。

segments.src: All else equal, what happens to EOQ?
segments.tr: 在其他条件不变的情况下，EOQ 会发生什么变化？

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) Raising your target service level from 95% to 99% increases required safety stock by only about 4%.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) 将目标服务水平从 95% 提高到 99% 仅需增加约 4% 的安全库存。

segments.src: **Q3.** Your average daily demand is 50 units, lead time is 6 days, and safety stock is 80 units.
segments.tr: **Q3.** 你的平均日需求量为 50 个，提前期为 6 天，安全库存为 80 个。

segments.src: - **Ordering cost (S)** — the fixed cost of placing and receiving one replenishment order, largely independent of order size.
segments.tr: - **订购成本 (S)** — 下达和接收一次补货订单的固定成本，基本与订单规模无关。

segments.src: - **Holding cost (H)** — the annual cost of keeping one unit in stock: space, capital, insurance, shrinkage, and obsolescence.
segments.tr: - **持有成本 (H)** — 每年持有一件库存的成本：空间、资金、保险、损耗和过时风险。

segments.src: - **EOQ (Economic Order Quantity)** — the order size that minimizes total ordering plus holding cost, equal to `sqrt(2DS/H)`.
segments.tr: - **EOQ (经济订货量)** — 使订购成本与持有成本之和最小化的订单规模，等于 `sqrt(2DS/H)`。

segments.src: - **Safety stock** — extra inventory held to absorb demand and lead-time variability, sized by your chosen service level.
segments.tr: - **安全库存** — 为吸收需求和提前期波动而持有的额外库存，其规模由你选择的服务水平决定。

segments.src: - **Reorder point (ROP)** — the stock level that triggers a new order: expected demand during lead time plus safety stock.
segments.tr: - **再订货点 (ROP)** — 触发新订单的库存水平：提前期内的预期需求加上安全库存。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** EOQ moves with the square root of S, so cutting S to 1/4 cuts EOQ to sqrt(1/4) = 1/2.
segments.tr: *答案：**Q1 — B.** EOQ 随 S 的平方根变化，因此将 S 降至 1/4 会使 EOQ 降至 sqrt(1/4) = 1/2。

segments.src: You'd order half as much, twice as often.
segments.tr: 你会以两倍的频率订购一半的数量。

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** The z-value goes from 1.65 to 2.33, so safety stock rises about 41%, not 4%.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (错误)。** z 值从 1.65 变为 2.33，因此安全库存上升了约 41%，而不是 4%。

segments.src: The last few points of service level are always the costliest.
segments.tr: 最后几个点的服务水平提升总是最昂贵的。

hi.title: [लॉजिस्टिक 101 #4] आपका वेयरहाउस असल में एक बैंक खाता क्यों है

segments.src: > Inventory is cash sitting on a shelf — and inventory management is the math of deciding how much cash to park there, and when to top it up.
segments.tr: > इन्वेंट्री शेल्फ पर रखा हुआ नकद है — और इन्वेंट्री मैनेजमेंट यह तय करने का गणित है कि वहाँ कितना नकद रखना है, और इसे कब दोबारा भरना है।

segments.src: Every unit in a warehouse is money you already spent but haven't earned back yet.
segments.tr: वेयरहाउस में मौजूद हर यूनिट वह पैसा है जिसे आप पहले ही खर्च कर चुके हैं लेकिन अभी तक वापस नहीं कमाया है।

segments.src: That's why inventory decisions are financial decisions dressed up as operational ones.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि इन्वेंट्री के निर्णय ऑपरेशनल निर्णय जैसे दिखने वाले वित्तीय निर्णय होते हैं।

segments.src: There are three costs constantly pulling against each other:
segments.tr: लगातार एक-दूसरे के विपरीत काम करने वाले तीन खर्च हैं:

segments.src: - **Ordering cost** — the fixed cost of placing one replenishment order: purchasing labor, freight setup, receiving, inspection. It's roughly the same whether you order 100 units or 1,000.
segments.tr: - **ऑर्डरिंग कॉस्ट (Ordering cost)** — एक पुनःपूर्ति ऑर्डर देने की निश्चित लागत: क्रaying श्रम, फ्रेट सेटअप, प्राप्त करना, निरीक्षण। यह लगभग समान है चाहे आप 100 यूनिट का ऑर्डर दें या 1,000 का।

segments.src: - **Holding (carrying) cost** — the cost of keeping a unit on the shelf for a year: warehouse space, insurance, shrinkage, obsolescence, and the capital tied up. A common rule of thumb is 20–30% of the item's cost per year.
segments.tr: - **होल्डिंग कॉस्ट (Holding cost)** — एक यूनिट को एक साल तक शेल्फ पर रखने की लागत: वेयरहाउस स्पेस, बीमा, क्षति, अप्रचलन, और फंसी हुई पूंजी। एक आम नियम यह है कि यह प्रति वर्ष वस्तु की लागत का 20–30% होती है।

segments.src: - **Stockout cost** — the sale you lose, the expedited freight you pay, the customer who goes elsewhere.
segments.tr: - **स्टॉकआउट कॉस्ट (Stockout cost)** — वह बिक्री जो आप खो देते हैं, वह त्वरित माल भाड़ा जिसका आप भुगतान करते हैं, वह ग्राहक जो कहीं और चला जाता है।

segments.src: Order in big batches and your ordering cost per unit drops, but your shelves fill up and holding cost climbs.
segments.tr: बड़े बैच में ऑर्डर करें और प्रति यूनिट आपकी ऑर्डरिंग कॉस्ट कम हो जाती है, लेकिन आपकी शेल्फ भर जाती हैं और होल्डिंग कॉस्ट बढ़ जाती है।

segments.src: Order in small batches and holding cost drops, but you're paying for orders constantly and flirting with stockouts.
segments.tr: छोटे बैच में ऑर्डर करें और होल्डिंग कॉस्ट कम हो जाती है, लेकिन आप लगातार ऑर्डर के लिए भुगतान कर रहे हैं और स्टॉकआउट के करीब पहुँच रहे हैं।

segments.src: Inventory management is finding the balance point.
segments.tr: इन्वेंट्री मैनेजमेंट संतुलन बिंदु ढूंढना है।

segments.src: **The EOQ model** answers "how much per order?"
segments.tr: **ईओक्यू मॉडल (EOQ model)** "प्रति ऑर्डर कितना?" का उत्तर देता है।

segments.tr: इकोनॉमिक ऑर्डर क्वांटिटी (Economic Order Quantity) वह बैच साइज़ है जहाँ वार्षिक ऑर्डरिंग कॉस्ट और वार्षिक होल्डिंग कॉस्ट बराबर होती हैं — कुल-लागत वक्र का निचला हिस्सा:

es.title: [Logística 101 #4] Por qué su almacén es en realidad una cuenta bancaria

segments.src: > Inventory is cash sitting on a shelf — and inventory management is the math of deciding how much cash to park there, and when to top it up.
segments.tr: > El inventario es dinero en efectivo sentado en un estante, y la gestión de inventario es el cálculo matemático para decidir cuánto efectivo estacionar allí y cuándo reponerlo.

segments.src: Every unit in a warehouse is money you already spent but haven't earned back yet.
segments.tr: Cada unidad en un almacén es dinero que ya gastó pero que aún no ha recuperado.

segments.src: That's why inventory decisions are financial decisions dressed up as operational ones.
segments.tr: Es por eso que las decisiones de inventario son decisiones financieras disfrazadas de operativas.

segments.src: There are three costs constantly pulling against each other:
segments.tr: Hay tres costos que se contraponen constantemente:

segments.src: - **Ordering cost** — the fixed cost of placing one replenishment order: purchasing labor, freight setup, receiving, inspection. It's roughly the same whether you order 100 units or 1,000.
segments.tr: - **Costo de pedido** — el costo fijo de realizar un pedido de reabastecimiento: mano de obra de compra, configuración de flete, recepción, inspección. Es aproximadamente el mismo si pide 100 unidades o 1,000.

segments.src: - **Holding (carrying) cost** — the cost of keeping a unit on the shelf for a year: warehouse space, insurance, shrinkage, obsolescence, and the capital tied up. A common rule of thumb is 20–30% of the item's cost per year.
segments.tr: - **Costo de mantenimiento (almacenamiento)** — el costo de mantener una unidad en el estante durante un año: espacio de almacén, seguros, mermas, obsolescencia y el capital inmovilizado. Una regla general común es el 20–30% del costo del artículo por año.

segments.src: - **Stockout cost** — the sale you lose, the expedited freight you pay, the customer who goes elsewhere.
segments.tr: - **Costo de falta de existencias (stockout)** — la venta que pierde, el flete urgente que paga, el cliente que se va a otra parte.

segments.src: Order in big batches and your ordering cost per unit drops, but your shelves fill up and holding cost climbs.
segments.tr: Si pide en lotes grandes, su costo de pedido por unidad disminuye, pero sus estantes se llenan y el costo de mantenimiento aumenta.

segments.src: Order in small batches and holding cost drops, but you're paying for orders constantly and flirting with stockouts.
segments.tr: Si pide en lotes pequeños, el costo de mantenimiento disminuye, pero paga constantemente por pedidos y coquetea con la falta de existencias.

segments.src: Inventory management is finding the balance point.
segments.tr: La gestión de inventario consiste en encontrar el punto de equilibrio.

segments.src: **The EOQ model** answers "how much per order?"
segments.tr: **El modelo EOQ** responde a "¿cuánto por pedido?"

segments.src: Economic Order Quantity is the batch size where annual ordering cost and annual holding cost are equal — the bottom of the total-cost curve:
segments.tr: La Cantidad Económica de Pedido (EOQ) es el tamaño de lote donde el costo anual de pedido y el costo anual de mantenimiento son iguales: el punto más bajo de la curva de costo total:

segments.src: S = cost to place one order ($)
segments.tr: S = cost to place one order ($)

segments.src: H = cost to hold one unit for one year ($)
segments.tr: H = cost to hold one unit for one year ($)

segments.src: Double your demand and EOQ doesn't double — it grows by about 41%.
segments.tr: Duplique su demanda y el EOQ no se duplica, crece aproximadamente un 41%.

segments.src: That's the mathematical reason big retailers hold proportionally *less* inventory than small ones, not more.
segments.tr: Esa es la razón matemática por la que los grandes minoristas mantienen proporcionalmente *menos* inventario que los pequeños, no más.
**El stock de seguridad** responde a "¿cuánta reserva?"

segments.src: EOQ assumes demand and lead times are perfectly predictable.
segments.tr: El EOQ asume que la demanda y los tiempos de entrega son perfectamente predecibles.

segments.src: Safety stock is the buffer you carry against that uncertainty:
segments.tr: El stock de seguridad es el amortiguador que usted lleva contra esa incertidumbre:

segments.src: Safety stock = z * (demand std deviation per day) * sqrt(lead time in days)
segments.tr: Safety stock = z * (demand std deviation per day) * sqrt(lead time in days)

segments.src: The `z` is your chosen **service level** — how often you're willing to be in stock when a customer arrives.
segments.tr: La `z` es su **nivel de servicio** elegido: qué tan dispuesto está a tener existencias cuando llega un cliente.
z ≈ 1.65 para el 95%, z ≈ 2.33 para el 99%.

segments.src: That jump is the expensive part: going from 95% to 99% costs about 41% more safety stock.
segments.tr: Ese salto es la parte costosa: pasar del 95% al 99% cuesta aproximadamente un 41% más en stock de seguridad.

segments.src: Chasing 100% costs infinite inventory, which is why nobody sane targets it.
segments.tr: Perseguir el 100% cuesta un inventario infinito, por lo que nadie en su sano juicio apunta a eso.

segments.src: **The reorder point** answers "when do I order?"
segments.tr: **El punto de pedido** responde a "¿cuándo hago el pedido?"

segments.src: It's the shelf level that triggers a new purchase order:
segments.tr: Es el nivel de estante que activa una nueva orden de compra:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: In plain English: enough to cover normal sales while the truck is en route, plus a cushion for the days that aren't normal.
segments.tr: En palabras simples: suficiente para cubrir las ventas normales mientras el camión está en camino, más una reserva para los días que no son normales.

segments.src: Say you run a small e-commerce brand out of Columbus, Ohio, selling an insulated water bottle.
segments.tr: Supongamos que dirige una pequeña marca de comercio electrónico desde Columbus, Ohio, vendiendo una botella de agua aislada.

segments.src: **The numbers:** you sell 12,000 units a year.
Each purchase order from your supplier costs about $75 in labor and paperwork.
segments.tr: Cada orden de compra de su proveedor cuesta alrededor de $75 en mano de obra y papeleo.

segments.src: Holding one bottle for a year costs $6 (warehouse space, capital, the risk it goes out of style).
segments.tr: Mantener una botella durante un año cuesta $6 (espacio de almacén, capital, el riesgo de que pase de moda).

segments.src: So about 548 bottles per order, or roughly 22 orders a year — one every two and a half weeks.
segments.tr: Así que alrededor de 548 botellas por pedido, o aproximadamente 22 pedidos al año, uno cada dos semanas y media.

segments.src: Your combined ordering + holding cost lands near $3,286 a year ($1,643 each, split evenly — that's the signature of being at the EOQ).
segments.tr: Su costo combinado de pedido + mantenimiento se sitúa cerca de $3,286 al año ($1,643 cada uno, dividido equitativamente; esa es la señal de estar en el EOQ).

segments.src: **When to order:** at 300 selling days a year, that's 40 bottles a day.
segments.tr: **Cuándo pedir:** con 300 días de venta al año, eso son 40 botellas al día.

segments.src: Your supplier's lead time is 7 days, so you'll sell about 280 bottles while you wait.
segments.tr: El tiempo de entrega de su proveedor es de 7 días, por lo que venderá unas 280 botellas mientras espera.

segments.tr: La demanda diaria oscila con una desviación estándar de unas 12 unidades, y usted quiere un nivel de servicio del 95%:

segments.src: Now you have a rule a warehouse associate can actually follow: **when the bin hits 333 bottles, order 548 more.** No meetings, no guessing.
segments.tr: Ahora tiene una regla que un asociado de almacén realmente puede seguir: **cuando el contenedor llegue a 333 botellas, pida 548 más.** Sin reuniones, sin adivinanzas.

segments.src: One comforting fact: the total-cost curve near EOQ is remarkably flat.
segments.tr: Un hecho reconfortante: la curva de costo total cerca del EOQ es notablemente plana.

segments.src: Order 20% more than the EOQ — say a 660-unit pallet instead of 548 — and your total cost rises less than 2%.
segments.tr: Pida un 20% más que el EOQ (digamos un palé de 660 unidades en lugar de 548) y su costo total aumenta menos del 2%.

segments.src: So if your supplier sells in full pallets or offers a volume discount, take the round number.
segments.tr: Así que si su proveedor vende en palés completos u ofrece un descuento por volumen, tome el número redondo.

segments.tr: El EOQ le da el vecindario; no exige precisión a la unidad.

fr.title: [Logistique 101 #4] Pourquoi votre entrepôt est réellement un compte bancaire

segments.src: > Inventory is cash sitting on a shelf — and inventory management is the math of deciding how much cash to park there, and when to top it up.
segments.tr: > Les stocks sont de l'argent immobilisé sur une étagère — et la gestion des stocks est le calcul qui consiste à décider combien d'argent y placer, et quand le réapprovisionner.

segments.src: Every unit in a warehouse is money you already spent but haven't earned back yet.
segments.tr: Chaque unité dans un entrepôt représente de l'argent que vous avez déjà dépensé mais que vous n'avez pas encore récupéré.

segments.src: That's why inventory decisions are financial decisions dressed up as operational ones.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi les décisions de stock sont des décisions financières déguisées en décisions opérationnelles.

segments.src: There are three costs constantly pulling against each other:
segments.tr: Il y a trois coûts qui s'opposent constamment :

segments.src: - **Ordering cost** — the fixed cost of placing one replenishment order: purchasing labor, freight setup, receiving, inspection. It's roughly the same whether you order 100 units or 1,000.
segments.tr: - **Coût de commande** — le coût fixe lié au passage d'une commande de réapprovisionnement : main-d'œuvre d'achat, mise en place du transport, réception, inspection. Il est à peu près identique, que vous commandiez 100 ou 1 000 unités.

segments.src: - **Holding (carrying) cost** — the cost of keeping a unit on the shelf for a year: warehouse space, insurance, shrinkage, obsolescence, and the capital tied up. A common rule of thumb is 20–30% of the item's cost per year.
segments.tr: - **Coût de possession (stockage)** — le coût de maintien d'une unité sur l'étagère pendant un an : espace d'entrepôt, assurance, démarque, obsolescence et capital immobilisé. Une règle empirique courante est de 20 à 30 % du coût de l'article par an.

segments.src: - **Stockout cost** — the sale you lose, the expedited freight you pay, the customer who goes elsewhere.
segments.tr: - **Coût de rupture de stock** — la vente que vous perdez, le fret express que vous payez, le client qui va voir ailleurs.

segments.src: Order in big batches and your ordering cost per unit drops, but your shelves fill up and holding cost climbs.
segments.tr: Commandez par gros lots et votre coût de commande par unité diminue, mais vos étagères se remplissent et le coût de possession augmente.

segments.src: Order in small batches and holding cost drops, but you're paying for orders constantly and flirting with stockouts.
segments.tr: Commandez par petits lots et le coût de possession diminue, mais vous payez constamment pour des commandes et vous flirtez avec les ruptures de stock.

segments.src: > Inventory is cash sitting on a shelf — and inventory management is the math of deciding how much cash to park there, and when to top it up.

segments.src: That's why inventory decisions are financial decisions dressed up as operational ones.

segments.src: There are three costs constantly pulling against each other:
segments.tr: Ada tiga biaya yang terus-menerus saling tarik-menarik:

segments.src: - **Ordering cost** — the fixed cost of placing one replenishment order: purchasing labor, freight setup, receiving, inspection. It's roughly the same whether you order 100 units or 1,000.
segments.tr: - **Biaya pemesanan (Ordering cost)** — biaya tetap untuk melakukan satu pesanan pengisian ulang: tenaga kerja pembelian, pengaturan pengiriman, penerimaan, inspeksi. Kurang lebih sama apakah Anda memesan 100 unit atau 1.000.

segments.src: - **Holding (carrying) cost** — the cost of keeping a unit on the shelf for a year: warehouse space, insurance, shrinkage, obsolescence, and the capital tied up. A common rule of thumb is 20–30% of the item's cost per year.
segments.tr: - **Biaya penyimpanan (Holding/carrying cost)** — biaya untuk menjaga satu unit di rak selama setahun: ruang gudang, asuransi, penyusutan, keusangan, dan modal yang tertahan. Aturan praktis yang umum adalah 20–30% dari biaya barang per tahun.

segments.src: - **Stockout cost** — the sale you lose, the expedited freight you pay, the customer who goes elsewhere.
segments.tr: - **Biaya kehabisan stok (Stockout cost)** — penjualan yang hilang, pengiriman kilat yang harus Anda bayar, pelanggan yang beralih ke tempat lain.

ja.title: [ロジスティクス 101 #4] なぜあなたの倉庫は実質的に銀行口座なのか

segments.src: > Inventory is cash sitting on a shelf — and inventory management is the math of deciding how much cash to park there, and when to top it up.
segments.tr: > 在庫は棚の上にある現金であり、在庫管理とはそこにどれだけの現金を置き、いつ補充するかを決める計算のことである。

segments.src: Every unit in a warehouse is money you already spent but haven't earned back yet.
segments.tr: 倉庫内のすべてのユニットは、すでに使ったもののまだ回収できていないお金である。

segments.src: That's why inventory decisions are financial decisions dressed up as operational ones.
segments.tr: そのため、在庫に関する決定は、業務上の決定に見せかけた財務上の決定なのだ。

segments.src: There are three costs constantly pulling against each other:
segments.tr: 常にお互いを引っ張り合っている3つのコストがある：

segments.src: - **Ordering cost** — the fixed cost of placing one replenishment order: purchasing labor, freight setup, receiving, inspection. It's roughly the same whether you order 100 units or 1,000.
segments.tr: - **発注費用 (Ordering cost)** — 1回分の補充発注を行うための固定費：購入時の人件費、輸送の手配、受入、検品。100個発注しても1,000個発注しても、ほぼ同じである。

segments.src: - **Holding (carrying) cost** — the cost of keeping a unit on the shelf for a year: warehouse space, insurance, shrinkage, obsolescence, and the capital tied up. A common rule of thumb is 20–30% of the item's cost per year.
segments.tr: - **保管費用 (Holding cost)** — 1つのユニットを1年間棚に置いておくためのコスト：倉庫のスペース、保険、目減り、陳腐化、およびロックされた資本。一般的な目安は、アイテムのコストの年間20〜30%である。

segments.src: - **Stockout cost** — the sale you lose, the expedited freight you pay, the customer who goes elsewhere.
segments.tr: - **欠品費用 (Stockout cost)** — 失われた売上、支払うことになった特急輸送費、他の店に行ってしまった顧客。

segments.src: Order in big batches and your ordering cost per unit drops, but your shelves fill up and holding cost climbs.
segments.tr: 大ロットで発注すれば1個あたりの発注費用は下がるが、棚が埋まって保管費用は上がる。

segments.src: Order in small batches and holding cost drops, but you're paying for orders constantly and flirting with stockouts.
segments.tr: 小ロットで発注すれば保管費用は下がるが、ひっきりなしに発注費用を払い、欠品の危険にさらされることになる。

segments.src: Inventory management is finding the balance point.
segments.tr: 在庫管理とは、そのバランス点を見つけることである。

segments.src: **The EOQ model** answers "how much per order?"
segments.tr: **EOQモデル (経済発注量モデル)** は「1回あたりいくつ発注すべきか？」に答える。

segments.src: Economic Order Quantity is the batch size where annual ordering cost and annual holding cost are equal — the bottom of the total-cost curve:
segments.tr: 経済発注量 (Economic Order Quantity) とは、年間発注費用と年間保管費用が等しくなる発注バッチサイズであり、総費用曲線の底にあたる：

segments.src: S = cost to place one order ($)
segments.tr: S = cost to place one order ($)

segments.src: H = cost to hold one unit for one year ($)
segments.tr: H = cost to hold one unit for one year ($)
平方根に注目してほしい。

segments.src: Double your demand and EOQ doesn't double — it grows by about 41%.
segments.tr: 需要が倍になってもEOQは倍にはならず、約41%増加するだけである。

segments.src: That's the mathematical reason big retailers hold proportionally *less* inventory than small ones, not more.
segments.tr: これが、大手小売店が小型店よりも比例して*少ない*在庫しか持たない数学的理由であり、多いわけではない。
**安全在庫 (Safety stock)** は「どれだけのクッションが必要か？」に答える。

segments.src: EOQ assumes demand and lead times are perfectly predictable.
segments.tr: EOQは、需要とリードタイムが完全に予測可能であると仮定している。

segments.src: Safety stock is the buffer you carry against that uncertainty:
segments.tr: 安全在庫とは、その不確実性に対して保有する緩衝材である：

segments.src: Safety stock = z * (demand std deviation per day) * sqrt(lead time in days)
segments.tr: Safety stock = z * (demand std deviation per day) * sqrt(lead time in days)

segments.src: The `z` is your chosen **service level** — how often you're willing to be in stock when a customer arrives.
segments.tr: この `z` は、あなたが選択した**サービス水準 (service level)** ——顧客が到着したときに在庫がある状態をどれだけの頻度で維持したいかである。
95%の場合は z ≈ 1.65、99%の場合は z ≈ 2.33 となる。

segments.src: That jump is the expensive part: going from 95% to 99% costs about 41% more safety stock.
segments.tr: その跳ね上がりがコストのかかる部分であり、95%から99%へ引き上げると、約41%多くの安全在庫が必要になる。

segments.src: Chasing 100% costs infinite inventory, which is why nobody sane targets it.
segments.tr: 100%を追求すると無限の在庫が必要になるため、正気の沙汰でそれを目標にする人はいない。

segments.src: **The reorder point** answers "when do I order?"
segments.tr: **発注点 (The reorder point)** は「いつ発注すべきか？」に答える。

segments.src: It's the shelf level that triggers a new purchase order:
segments.tr: それは新しい発注書をトリガーする棚の在庫水準である：

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: In plain English: enough to cover normal sales while the truck is en route, plus a cushion for the days that aren't normal.
segments.tr: 分かりやすく言えば：トラックが移動中である通常の売上をカバーするのに十分な量に加え、正常ではない日々のためのクッションである。

segments.src: Say you run a small e-commerce brand out of Columbus, Ohio, selling an insulated water bottle.
segments.tr: オハイオ州コロンバスで断熱ウォーターボトルを販売する小さなEコマースブランドを運営しているとしよう。

segments.src: **The numbers:** you sell 12,000 units a year.
segments.tr: **数値：** 年間12,000個を販売する。

segments.src: Each purchase order from your supplier costs about $75 in labor and paperwork.
segments.tr: サプライヤーからの各発注書には、人件費と事務作業で約75ドルのコストがかかる。

segments.src: Holding one bottle for a year costs $6 (warehouse space, capital, the risk it goes out of style).
segments.tr: 1本のボトルを1年間保管するコストは6ドル（倉庫スペース、資本、時代遅れになるリスク）である。

segments.src: So about 548 bottles per order, or roughly 22 orders a year — one every two and a half weeks.
segments.tr: つまり、1回あたり約548本、年間で約22回発注することになり、2週間半に1回のペースとなる。

segments.src: Your combined ordering + holding cost lands near $3,286 a year ($1,643 each, split evenly — that's the signature of being at the EOQ).
segments.tr: 発注費用と保管費用を合わせると年間約3,286ドル（それぞれ1,643ドルずつ均等に分割。これがEOQにいることの証拠である）に着地する。

segments.src: **When to order:** at 300 selling days a year, that's 40 bottles a day.
segments.tr: **いつ発注するか：** 年間300営業日として、1日あたり40本となる。

segments.src: Your supplier's lead time is 7 days, so you'll sell about 280 bottles while you wait.
segments.tr: サプライヤーのリードタイムは7日なので、待っている間に約280本が売れる。

segments.src: Daily demand swings with a standard deviation of about 12 units, and you want a 95% service level:
segments.tr: 日々の需要は標準偏差約12ユニットで変動し、95%のサービス水準を望む場合：

segments.src: Now you have a rule a warehouse associate can actually follow: **when the bin hits 333 bottles, order 548 more.** No meetings, no guessing.
segments.tr: これで倉庫の従業員が実際に従うことができるルールができる：**ビンが333本に達したら、さらに548本を発注する。** 会議も推測も不要だ。

segments.src: One comforting fact: the total-cost curve near EOQ is remarkably flat.
segments.tr: 1つ安心できる事実として、EOQ付近の総費用曲線は非常に平坦である。

segments.src: Order 20% more than the EOQ — say a 660-unit pallet instead of 548 — and your total cost rises less than 2%.
segments.tr: EOQより20%多く発注する（548本の代わりに660個のパレットなど）場合でも、総費用の増加は2%未満である。

segments.src: So if your supplier sells in full pallets or offers a volume discount, take the round number.
segments.tr: したがって、サプライヤーがパレット単位で販売している場合やボリュームディスカウントを提供している場合は、キリの良い数字を採用すればよい。

segments.src: EOQ gives you the neighborhood; it doesn't demand precision to the unit.
segments.tr: EOQは近辺の値を教えてくれるものであり、1個単位の正確さを要求するものではない。
そして、このモデルの限界を知っておくこと。

segments.src: EOQ assumes steady demand, a fixed lead time, no quantity discounts, and unlimited storage.
segments.tr: EOQは、安定した需要、固定されたリードタイム、数量割引なし、無制限の保管スペースを仮定している。

segments.src: Real life breaks all four — seasonal spikes, port delays, case-pack minimums.
segments.tr: 現実の生活ではそのすべてが崩れる――季節的な急増、港の遅延、ケースパックの最小要件など。

segments.src: Treat EOQ as a sanity check on your ordering habits, not as gospel.
segments.tr: EOQは発注習慣の正気度チェックとして扱い、絶対的な真理として扱わないこと。

segments.src: 1. Inventory is a tug-of-war between ordering cost (favors big batches) and holding cost (favors small ones); EOQ is where they balance, and it scales with the *square root* of demand.
segments.tr: 1. 在庫は発注費用（大ロットびいき）と保管費用（小ロットびいき）の綱引きであり、EOQはそのバランスが取れる場所であり、需要の*平方根*に比例してスケールする。

segments.src: 2. Safety stock buys protection against uncertainty, and the price of that protection rises steeply as you approach 100% service — 95% to 99% costs about 41% more stock.
segments.tr: 2. 安全在庫は不確実性に対する保護を買うものであり、その保護の価格は100%のサービスに近づくにつれて急激に上昇する（95%から99%への引き上げは約41%多くの在庫コストがかかる）。

segments.src: 3. The reorder point turns all of it into one simple floor-level rule: demand during lead time, plus your cushion.
segments.tr: 3. 発注点は、そのすべてを1つのシンプルな現場のルールに変える：リードタイム中の需要とクッションの足し算である。

segments.src: **Q1.** Your supplier streamlines the process and your ordering cost `S` drops to one-quarter of what it was.
segments.tr: **Q1.** サプライヤーがプロセスを効率化し、発注費用 `S` が以前の4分の1に低下した。

segments.src: All else equal, what happens to EOQ?
segments.tr: 他の条件が同じである場合、EOQはどうなるか？

segments.src: **Q2.** (O/X) Raising your target service level from 95% to 99% increases required safety stock by only about 4%.
segments.tr: **Q2.** (O/X) 目標サービス水準を95%から99%に引き上げると、必要な安全在庫は約4%しか増加しない。

segments.src: **Q3.** Your average daily demand is 50 units, lead time is 6 days, and safety stock is 80 units.
segments.tr: **Q3.** あなたの平均日次需要は50ユニット、リードタイムは6日、安全在庫は80ユニットである。
発注点はいくつになるか？

segments.src: - **Ordering cost (S)** — the fixed cost of placing and receiving one replenishment order, largely independent of order size.
segments.tr: - **発注費用 (S)** — 1回の補充発注を行い、受け取るための固定費であり、発注サイズとはほぼ無関係である。

segments.src: - **Holding cost (H)** — the annual cost of keeping one unit in stock: space, capital, insurance, shrinkage, and obsolescence.
segments.tr: - **保管費用 (H)** — 1つのユニットを在庫として保持しておく年間コスト：スペース、資本、保険、目減り、陳腐化。

segments.src: - **EOQ (Economic Order Quantity)** — the order size that minimizes total ordering plus holding cost, equal to `sqrt(2DS/H)`.
segments.tr: - **EOQ (経済発注量)** — 総発注費用と保管費用を最小化する発注サイズであり、`sqrt(2DS/H)` に等しい。

segments.src: - **Safety stock** — extra inventory held to absorb demand and lead-time variability, sized by your chosen service level.
segments.tr: - **安全在庫** — 需要とリードタイムの変動を吸収するために保持される追加の在庫であり、選択したサービス水準によってサイズが決まる。

segments.src: - **Reorder point (ROP)** — the stock level that triggers a new order: expected demand during lead time plus safety stock.
segments.tr: - **発注点 (ROP)** — 新しい発注をトリガーする在庫水準：リードタイム中の予想需要に安全在庫を加えたもの。

segments.src: *Answers: **Q1 — B.** EOQ moves with the square root of S, so cutting S to 1/4 cuts EOQ to sqrt(1/4) = 1/2.
segments.tr: *回答: **Q1 — B.** EOQはSの平方根とともに動くため、Sを1/4にカットするとEOQは sqrt(1/4) = 1/2 にカットされる。

segments.src: You'd order half as much, twice as often.
segments.tr: 半分量を、2倍の頻度で発注することになる。

segments.src: **Q2 — X (false).** The z-value goes from 1.65 to 2.33, so safety stock rises about 41%, not 4%.
segments.tr: **Q2 — X (偽).** z値が1.65から2.33に移行するため、安全在庫は約4%ではなく約41%増加する。

segments.src: The last few points of service level are always the costliest.
segments.tr: サービス水準の最後の数ポイントは常に最もコストがかかる。

vi.title: [Logistics 101 #4] Tại sao kho hàng của bạn thực chất là một tài khoản ngân hàng

segments.src: > Inventory is cash sitting on a shelf — and inventory management is the math of deciding how much cash to park there, and when to top it up.
segments.tr: > Hàng tồn kho chính là tiền mặt đang nằm trên kệ — và quản lý hàng tồn kho là bài toán quyết định xem nên để bao nhiêu tiền mặt ở đó, và khi nào thì cần bổ sung thêm.

segments.src: Every unit in a warehouse is money you already spent but haven't earned back yet.
segments.tr: Mỗi đơn vị hàng trong kho là số tiền bạn đã chi ra nhưng chưa thu hồi lại được.

segments.src: That's why inventory decisions are financial decisions dressed up as operational ones.
segments.tr: Đó là lý do tại sao các quyết định về hàng tồn kho thực chất là các quyết định tài chính được ngụy trang dưới hình thức vận hành.

segments.src: There are three costs constantly pulling against each other:
segments.tr: Có ba loại chi phí luôn đối nghịch nhau:

segments.src: - **Ordering cost** — the fixed cost of placing one replenishment order: purchasing labor, freight setup, receiving, inspection. It's roughly the same whether you order 100 units or 1,000.
segments.tr: - **Chi phí đặt hàng (Ordering cost)** — chi phí cố định cho một đơn hàng bổ sung: nhân công mua hàng, thiết lập vận chuyển, tiếp nhận, kiểm tra. Chi phí này gần như không đổi dù bạn đặt 100 hay 1.000 đơn vị.

segments.src: - **Holding (carrying) cost** — the cost of keeping a unit on the shelf for a year: warehouse space, insurance, shrinkage, obsolescence, and the capital tied up. A common rule of thumb is 20–30% of the item's cost per year.
segments.tr: - **Chi phí lưu kho (Holding/carrying cost)** — chi phí để giữ một đơn vị hàng trên kệ trong một năm: không gian kho bãi, bảo hiểm, hao hụt, lỗi thời và vốn bị chiếm dụng. Một quy tắc chung thường thấy là 20–30% giá trị của mặt hàng mỗi năm.

segments.src: - **Stockout cost** — the sale you lose, the expedited freight you pay, the customer who goes elsewhere.
segments.tr: - **Chi phí thiếu hàng (Stockout cost)** — doanh số bị mất, chi phí vận chuyển nhanh phải trả, khách hàng chuyển sang nơi khác.

segments.src: Order in big batches and your ordering cost per unit drops, but your shelves fill up and holding cost climbs.
segments.tr: Đặt hàng theo lô lớn thì chi phí đặt hàng trên mỗi đơn vị giảm xuống, nhưng kệ hàng sẽ đầy ắp và chi phí lưu kho tăng lên.

segments.src: Order in small batches and holding cost drops, but you're paying for orders constantly and flirting with stockouts.
segments.tr: Đặt hàng theo lô nhỏ thì chi phí lưu kho giảm, nhưng bạn phải trả phí đặt hàng liên tục và đối mặt với nguy cơ thiếu hàng.

segments.src: Inventory management is finding the balance point.
segments.tr: Quản lý hàng tồn kho chính là tìm ra điểm cân bằng đó.

segments.src: **The EOQ model** answers "how much per order?"
segments.tr: **Mô hình EOQ** trả lời cho câu hỏi "đặt bao nhiêu cho mỗi đơn hàng?"

segments.src: Economic Order Quantity is the batch size where annual ordering cost and annual holding cost are equal — the bottom of the total-cost curve:
segments.tr: Số lượng đặt hàng kinh tế (Economic Order Quantity) là quy mô lô hàng mà tại đó chi phí đặt hàng hàng năm và chi phí lưu kho hàng năm bằng nhau — điểm thấp nhất của đường cong tổng chi phí:

segments.src: S = cost to place one order ($)
segments.tr: S = cost to place one order ($)

segments.src: H = cost to hold one unit for one year ($)

segments.src: Double your demand and EOQ doesn't double — it grows by about 41%.
segments.tr: Nếu nhu cầu tăng gấp đôi thì EOQ không tăng gấp đôi — nó chỉ tăng khoảng 41%.

segments.src: That's the mathematical reason big retailers hold proportionally *less* inventory than small ones, not more.
segments.tr: Đó là lý do toán học giải thích tại sao các nhà bán lẻ lớn lại giữ tỷ lệ hàng tồn kho *ít hơn* so với các nhà bán lẻ nhỏ, chứ không phải nhiều hơn.
**Hàng tồn kho an toàn (Safety stock)** trả lời cho câu hỏi "cần bao nhiêu dự phòng?"

segments.src: EOQ assumes demand and lead times are perfectly predictable.
segments.tr: EOQ giả định rằng nhu cầu và thời gian chờ hàng (lead time) là hoàn toàn có thể dự đoán được.

segments.src: Safety stock is the buffer you carry against that uncertainty:
segments.tr: Hàng tồn kho an toàn là lớp đệm bạn duy trì để chống lại sự không chắc chắn đó:

segments.src: Safety stock = z * (demand std deviation per day) * sqrt(lead time in days)
segments.tr: Safety stock = z * (demand std deviation per day) * sqrt(lead time in days)

segments.src: The `z` is your chosen **service level** — how often you're willing to be in stock when a customer arrives.
segments.tr: Chữ `z` là **mức độ dịch vụ (service level)** bạn chọn — tần suất bạn muốn có sẵn hàng khi khách hàng đến mua.

segments.src: That jump is the expensive part: going from 95% to 99% costs about 41% more safety stock.
segments.tr: Bước nhảy đó chính là phần đắt đỏ: tăng từ 95% lên 99% khiến chi phí hàng tồn kho an toàn tăng thêm khoảng 41%.

segments.src: Chasing 100% costs infinite inventory, which is why nobody sane targets it.
segments.tr: Theo đuổi mức 100% sẽ tốn chi phí tồn kho vô hạn, đó là lý do không ai tỉnh táo lại đặt mục tiêu đó.

segments.src: **The reorder point** answers "when do I order?"
segments.tr: **Điểm đặt hàng lại (Reorder point)** trả lời cho câu hỏi "khi nào tôi nên đặt hàng?"

segments.src: It's the shelf level that triggers a new purchase order:
segments.tr: Đó là mức tồn kho trên kệ kích hoạt một đơn đặt hàng mới:

segments.src: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock
segments.tr: Reorder point = (average daily demand * lead time in days) + safety stock

segments.src: In plain English: enough to cover normal sales while the truck is en route, plus a cushion for the days that aren't normal.
segments.tr: Nói một cách đơn giản: đủ để đáp ứng doanh số bình thường trong khi xe tải đang trên đường vận chuyển, cộng thêm một khoản dự phòng cho những ngày không bình thường.

segments.src: Say you run a small e-commerce brand out of Columbus, Ohio, selling an insulated water bottle.
segments.tr: Giả sử bạn điều hành một thương hiệu thương mại điện tử nhỏ ở Columbus, Ohio, bán bình nước giữ nhiệt.

segments.src: **The numbers:** you sell 12,000 units a year.
segments.tr: **Các con số:** bạn bán được 12.000 đơn vị một năm.

segments.src: Each purchase order from your supplier costs about $75 in labor and paperwork.
segments.tr: Mỗi đơn đặt hàng từ nhà cung cấp tốn khoảng $75 cho nhân công và giấy tờ.

segments.src: Holding one bottle for a year costs $6 (warehouse space, capital, the risk it goes out of style).
segments.tr: Lưu kho một chiếc bình trong một năm tốn $6 (không gian kho, vốn, rủi ro lỗi thời).

segments.src: So about 548 bottles per order, or roughly 22 orders a year — one every two and a half weeks.
segments.tr: Vậy khoảng 548 bình mỗi đơn hàng, hoặc khoảng 22 đơn hàng một năm — mỗi hai tuần rưỡi một lần.

segments.src: Your combined ordering + holding cost lands near $3,286 a year ($1,643 each, split evenly — that's the signature of being at the EOQ).
segments.tr: Tổng chi phí đặt hàng + lưu kho của bạn rơi vào khoảng $3.286 một năm ($1.643 mỗi loại, chia đều — đó là dấu hiệu của việc đạt mức EOQ).

segments.src: **When to order:** at 300 selling days a year, that's 40 bottles a day.
segments.tr: **Khi nào đặt hàng:** với 300 ngày bán hàng một năm, tức là 40 bình một ngày.

segments.src: Now you have a rule a warehouse associate can actually follow: **when the bin hits 333 bottles, order 548 more.** No meetings, no guessing.
segments.tr: Bây giờ bạn có một quy tắc mà nhân viên kho thực sự có thể làm theo: **khi kho còn 333 bình, hãy đặt thêm 548 bình nữa.** Không cần họp hành, không cần đoán mò.

segments.src: One comforting fact: the total-cost curve near EOQ is remarkably flat.
segments.tr: Một sự thật an ủi: đường cong tổng chi phí gần mức EOQ khá phẳng.

segments.src: Order 20% more than the EOQ — say a 660-unit pallet instead of 548 — and your total cost rises less than 2%.
segments.tr: Đặt nhiều hơn 20% so với EOQ — ví dụ một pallet 660 đơn vị thay vì 548 — thì tổng chi phí của bạn chỉ tăng chưa đầy 2%.

segments.src: So if your supplier sells in full pallets or offers a volume discount, take the round number.
segments.tr: Vì vậy, nếu nhà cung cấp bán theo nguyên pallet hoặc có chiết khấu theo số lượng, hãy lấy con số tròn trịa.

segments.src: EOQ gives you the neighborhood; it doesn't demand precision to the unit.
segments.tr: EOQ chỉ cho bạn biết khu vực cần hướng tới; nó không yêu cầu độ chính xác đến từng đơn vị.
